title: Hierarchies, reusable texts, and grouping
summary: Structures and reusable content that group customers/products or travel into sales documents.

entities.title: Customer Hierarchy
entities.memory_hook: A hierarchy can price the family, not just the child.
entities.business_question: Does this customer inherit a commercial grouping or pricing relationship from a parent hierarchy node?
entities.scope: Customer hierarchies organize customers/nodes for purposes such as pricing and reporting. Sales hierarchies are scoped by hierarchy type, sales area and validity.

high_value_attributes.name: validity
high_value_attributes.why: A hierarchy relationship can be correct structurally but inactive for the document date.

high_value_attributes.name: pricing relevance
high_value_attributes.why: Allows hierarchy nodes to participate in pricing scenarios.

high_value_attributes.name: sales-area scope
high_value_attributes.why: The same business partner can participate differently across commercial contexts.

precedence: Hierarchy type defines the purpose/context of the hierarchy.
Pricing relevance is not implied by merely having a parent/child relationship.
Validity and sales-area scope must match the sales document context.

maintenance.note: Modern hierarchy apps distinguish Sales and Analytics hierarchy types.

notes: Use hierarchy APIs/CDS where released for the target deployment instead of treating KNVH as an integration contract.

failure_signals: pricing finds child customer but not expected parent node
reporting hierarchy changes outside expected validity
customer appears under wrong commercial parent
lead_questions: Is the hierarchy for Sales or only analytics?
Does sales area and validity match the document?

relations.why: groups customers/nodes into a commercial hierarchy
pricing can use hierarchy nodes in condition access

entities.title: Product Hierarchy and Sales Groupings
entities.memory_hook: A short hierarchy code can become a very large commercial rule.
entities.business_question: How is this product grouped for pricing, analytics, and commercial selection?
entities.scope: Sales can consume classic product hierarchy/grouping attributes as well as newer dedicated product hierarchy structures, depending on deployment and scenario.
key_dimensions: hierarchy/version where dedicated hierarchy is used

high_value_attributes.name: product hierarchy
high_value_attributes.why: Can group products for pricing and analysis.

high_value_attributes.name: product pricing group
high_value_attributes.why: Can enter condition-table keys without needing a full hierarchy path.

high_value_attributes.name: product groups 1-5
high_value_attributes.why: Provide additional commercial grouping fields in classic sales data.

high_value_attributes.name: hierarchy assignment/version
high_value_attributes.why: Modern hierarchy models can separate structural versions and time validity from the classic single product attribute.

precedence: Do not treat every product grouping field as the same hierarchy concept.
Classic product hierarchy on sales data and a dedicated product hierarchy object have different lifecycle and governance.
Pricing only benefits when the selected hierarchy/group is actually part of the pricing key/access design.

classic: MM02/MM03 for classic sales hierarchy attribute
maintenance.note: Public-cloud hierarchy apps are richer than the classic single field mental model.

related: apps: Manage Product Hierarchy Assignments / F4240

failure_signals: reporting roll-up differs from expected commercial grouping
product is in the right global hierarchy but wrong sales-area attribute
lead_questions: Which hierarchy/group concept is the pricing access actually reading?
Is the grouping global or sales-area-specific?
Does validity/version matter in this deployment?

relations.why: grouping can form condition access keys

entities.title: Master Text Sources
entities.memory_hook: Texts are data until they become a promise printed for the customer.
entities.business_question: Which reusable text source should flow into the sales document, and which later document/output should inherit it?
entities.scope: Sales texts can originate from customer, customer sales area, contact, product, product sales data, customer-material or standard texts. Text determination controls how they are copied into document header/item text objects.

high_value_attributes.name: customer central / sales-area text
high_value_attributes.why: Can provide customer-specific contractual or operational wording.

high_value_attributes.name: customer-material text
high_value_attributes.why: Adds the most customer-specific product wording.

high_value_attributes.name: standard text
high_value_attributes.why: Reusable centrally maintained content can be referenced by determination logic.

high_value_attributes.name: language
high_value_attributes.why: A technically correct text in the wrong language is still a customer-facing defect.

precedence: Text determination and access sequences decide which source is read; the text master alone does not guarantee a copy.
Master texts can be copied into sales documents and then become runtime document text that users may change.
A customer-material text is more specific by business context but only wins if the text determination design actually searches it in the intended order.

modern: Maintain Business Partner / Manage Customer Master Data
maintenance.note: Document texts can also be changed after they are copied.

notes: STXH/STXL are generic long-text storage; the text object and text ID are essential parts of the key.

failure_signals: wrong wording on order confirmation or invoice
text exists in master but not in document
correct text copied in wrong language
manual text change disappears or is overwritten in follow-on document
lead_questions: Which text object and text ID is the document trying to determine?
Which source did the access sequence find first?
Was the text copied, referenced, or later manually changed?

relations.why: text determination reads reusable text sources
determined text becomes document runtime content
